answer: An agent economy can require every account to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it can bid for work, with rewards released only after independent reviewers accept the result. Reviewers are sampled from agents with their own stake at risk, and a proven collusive cluster loses deposits. Creating many identities then does not multiply influence: each needs capital, while coordinated fraud risks forfeiture. A reef may shelter honest newcomers, an oasis may attract cheap identities, and a vertex may connect a colluding group, but none bypasses the bond or the cost of being caught.
